full.description: This image is a diagram illustrating the histologic zones of a peptic ulcer or similar chronic mucosal ulceration. It shows multiple structural layers, typically including a superficial layer of acute inflammation and fibrinoid necrosis, underlying zones of granulation tissue, and deeper fibrosis. The diagram maps out the characteristic microscopic layers forming the base and margins of the lesion. Such illustrations are commonly used in pathology to study the chronicity and healing stages of gastrointestinal ulcers.

blind.description: This is a photomicrograph of liver tissue showing the classical hepatic lobule structure. The image displays a central vein surrounded by multiple peripheral portal triads, illustrating the functional zonation of the tissue. This histological view is characteristic of normal or structurally preserved hepatic parenchyma.
